reason: The only available combination should let me harvest lettuce for the garden meal.
expectation: I expect to cut fresh leaves from the trough, though preparing the meal may take another step.

effect: The harvest produced lettuce leaves, so I can now take them to the galley for the meal.
reaction: Nothing notable; the harvest worked as expected.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley directly advances the goal of eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat the lettuce with the available meal.

alternatives.reason: I considered harvesting again, but I already have leaves to use.

effect: The galley action completed the meal and the chapter, connecting the garden harvest with the ongoing effort to keep the frozen discovery safe.
reaction: The detail of the two fans was a satisfying reminder of what the station is protecting during the storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing supper was most worthwhile: the fresh leaves made the effort to keep the garden alive feel tangible, while the fans recalled the frozen discovery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Harvesting the lettuce was predictable and produced no descriptive passage, though it was a natural step toward the meal.

surprise.text: The supper passage brought the cold case into the scene through the sound of its fan; I had expected the meal but not that connection.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: cutting leaves and taking them to the galley both had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to learn what happens to the body in the ice. This chapter's meal was quiet, but its mention of the case renewed that curiosity.
